title: Keeping AI Off the Deterministic Path — Check

questions.prompt: Why is Agronomy Studio's AI search implemented as a deterministic mock?
questions.explanation: A deterministic mock returns the same output for the same input, so the test suite can make stable assertions and the trustworthy core results never depend on a probabilistic component.
options: Because real LLMs are too cheap to bother with
So tests can assert exact outputs and the core results stay reproducible
To make the gateway slower on purpose
Because the frontend cannot parse model output

questions.prompt: In Agronomy Studio, the agronomic figures a user acts on are produced by the deterministic compute path, not by the AI component.
questions.explanation: True. The gateway and domain modules compute reproducible, traceable values; AI search sits beside that path as an advisory convenience, not inside it.

questions.prompt: What is the benefit of treating the AI search as a separate lib module behind its own surface?
questions.explanation: With AI isolated behind its own contract, replacing the stub with a real model is a contained change; the deterministic gateway path and its tests are unaffected.
options: It forces the gateway to call the model on every request
Swapping the stub for a real model later is a localized change that leaves the deterministic path and its tests untouched
It removes the need for type checking
It lets the frontend bypass the gateway

questions.prompt: What general principle does the AI design illustrate?
questions.explanation: The pattern is a deterministic, tested core with non-deterministic, advisory components at the edges, so failures cost a convenience rather than a correct answer.
options: Put all logic into the frontend
Push non-determinism to the edges and keep the core reproducible
Avoid testing anything that calls a network
Always prefer probabilistic answers over computed ones
